name: Cego
description: Cego: German Tarock from Baden; 3–4p, 54-card Cego deck (22 trumps + 32 in 4 suits). Central hand (Legage/Cego); many contracts use Legage. Developed from Ombre and Dreierles. Two-phase bidding; declarer may play from Cego (central hand); follow suit, must trump if unable to follow; 70 card points total, bidder needs 36+ to win normal contracts.

history.origins: Germany (Baden, Hohenzollern). Cego developed early 19th c. from Dreierles and Ombre (Napoleonic Wars). 54-card Cego deck; central hand (Legage). National game of Baden; only German region where genuine Tarok cards remain in general use.
timeline: Early 19th c.: Cego from Dreierles + Ombre
Baden/Hohenzollern; only German region with widespread Tarot

variations.name: Pflicht-Räuber
variations.description: Compulsory round of Räuber at fixed time (e.g. 23:00); one deal per player, no other bidding. Loser pays; if one player takes no tricks loser pays 60; stakes multiply after the round.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses same engine as base; overrides would need local stake and timing rules when documented.

variations.name: Ministranten Version
variations.description: Bräunlingen variant: Vorhand can choose Cego, Piccolo, Bettel, Geregelter Räuber, Wilder Räuber or Dresch when all pass. Stricter rules for Eine Leere / Zwei Leere (must lead exposed cards; bidder leads after first trick(s)).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds contract choices and lead rules; overrides require documented Bräunlingen rule set.

scoring.description: Card points in tricks: Gstieß, Trock 21, Trock 1, Kings 5 each; Queens 4; Cavaliers 3; Jacks 2; others 1. Total 70. Normal games: bidder needs 36+ (plus at least one trick). Count in threes, subtract 2 per group; remainder subtract 1. Special games (Ulti, Piccolo, Bettel, Räuber) have fixed scores.
scoring.winCondition: Normal games: bidder wins by taking at least 36 card points and at least one trick; defenders win otherwise. Special games: Ulti (last trick with Trock 1), Piccolo (exactly one trick), Bettel (no tricks), Räuber (lowest points wins).
